title: Suryoday Small Finance Bank Ltd - 543279 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Suryoday SFB Q1 FY27: GNPA 6.5%, NNPA 1.2% after INR387 crore CGFMU claim; ROA about 1.6% helped by INR46 crore PSL income.
summary.overview: Gross advances rose 32.5% YoY to INR14,376 crore and deposits rose 29.4% YoY to INR14,634 crore in Q1 FY27. Bank-level slippages fell to INR92 crore from INR106 crore QoQ, and MFI slippages fell to INR53 crore from INR73 crore. Other income was lifted by about INR90 crore of PSL/other income plus INR46 crore of PSL certificate sales (INR1,600 crore sold), which management said will not recur at this scale in Q2 and Q3. Management reiterated FY27 guidance: credit cost 0.8–1.0%, ROE 13–14% range, ROA of about 1.6% by Q4, and cost-to-income of 67–70%.

financial_highlights.change: Adjusted for INR134 crore CGFMU receivable: 2.9% / 0.3%

financial_highlights.value: Down about 8 bps QoQ; guided ~7.5% for rest of FY27

segments.name: Inclusive finance (MFI/JLG and individual loans)
segments.commentary: Current-bucket collection efficiency 99.2%, recent-cohort 99.4%. Individual loans are about 80% of monthly onboarding; IF share of advances fell to 44% from 48%. Slippages run below INR20 crore a month.

segments.name: Vehicle finance (CV)
segments.commentary: PAR rose to 11.5% from 10.1% QoQ, attributed to fuel prices and load availability. About 75–80% of the book is used CVs. Management expects normalisation from Q2/Q3 after monsoon.

segments.name: Mortgages and secured retail
segments.commentary: Secured retail growing 30–35% YoY. Mortgages present in under 25% of branches, targeted at 40–45% by year-end. Some mortgage slippages are being resolved through legal process.

segments.name: Digital (CLOU/UPI credit line, digital deposits, digital MSME)
segments.commentary: Digital deposits INR2,222 crore with average daily accretion of INR6 crore. UPI credit customers crossed 9 lakh; CLOU convenience fee income INR18 crore against about INR13 crore related cost. Digital MSME disbursements INR59 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 credit cost guided at 0.8–1.0%; Q1 at 0.8%.
Cost of funds around 7.5% for the rest of FY27; NIM expected to stay similar to the Q1 level.
ROA guided at about 1.6% in Q4 FY27 with no change to the start-of-year guidance; management said Q2 PSL income will be lower.
Steady-state ROE 13–14%, with a target of 0.5–1% YoY improvement over the next couple of years.
PSL income guided at INR10–15 crore in each of Q2 and Q3, and INR15–20 crore in Q4.

Opex (full-stack cost-to-income) target 67–70%; PAT guidance of INR300 crore-plus for FY27 referenced by an analyst; management said Q2 would be subdued, with about INR75 crore per quarter as the focus.
Yield on advances to stabilise at 17.2–17.5%; no immediate pricing change planned this quarter.
Capital adequacy about 20%, with a target of 20–22%. Fresh Tier 2 raise being explored with a target to close in Q2; Tier 1 raise under evaluation.
capex_capacity: About 50 branches to be added in Q2 and Q3 FY27, mainly for IF and CV expansion into new locations.
Mortgage presence to rise from under 25% of branches to 40–45% by year-end.

CLOU customer base about 6 lakh active users, with 9–10 lakh approved. Target to double active users to about 12 lakh this fiscal year. Onboarding 1.5–2 lakh customers a month, average ticket under INR5,000.
Remaining CGFMU claim of about INR15–20 crore due this year; a further INR135–150 crore claimable in subsequent years.
demand_pricing: Management said the MFI cycle has turned, but it is staying cautious on growth and will not treat the recovery as a reason to grow aggressively.
Advances are growing faster than deposits; MFI performing book grew about INR500 crore in one quarter.
IBPC funding reopened at roughly 5% after the MFI book improved.
Deposit costs: SA cost of funds 5.5% (from 5.7%); FD cost about 8.1%. FD rates have not eased.
VL (individual loan) yield about 25–25.25%; secured assets yield about 12%.
Management said the competition will be intense and the digital play is the differentiator.

qa_highlights.question: Other income of about INR147 crore looks high. What is the steady-state run-rate for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Other income included about INR90 crore of PSL income plus INR46 crore from selling INR1,600 crore of PSL certificates. Q2 and Q3 PSL income is expected at INR10–15 crore each, and Q4 at INR15–20 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 1.6% ROA reach 1.8–1.9% by Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 included about INR40 crore of PSL income, and the next two quarters will not have similar PSL opportunities, so the 1.6% ROA is not a base for linear increase.

qa_highlights.question: What happened to yield on non-NPA advances (17.2% to 16.1%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Mix shift away from IF (share down from 48% to 44%) cost about INR0.75 impact, and Q4 had higher MFI recovery income. Yield is expected to return to about 17%, and the stabilised range is 17.2–17.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did slippages stay elevated and what is the resolution path?
qa_highlights.answer: Bank-level slippages fell to INR92 crore from INR106 crore. Some mortgage cases are being resolved through legal process, and management expects these to come down in the coming quarter with well-collateralised assets.

qa_highlights.question: Why did CV PAR rise to 11.5% from 10.1%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the increase to higher fuel prices and load availability, with monsoon seasonality also adding to it. It expects PAR to settle back by Q2 and normalise by about September, and it has no geographic concentration in the book.

qa_highlights.question: Is the insurance model at risk if many lenders take cover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said insurance is a last-resort backstop and the bank is not using it as a shield for business. Norms will be tighter and premiums may exceed claims in the next couple of years; NCGTC is described as well funded.

risks_watch: CV PAR at 11.5% (from 10.1%) driven by fuel prices and load availability; monitor whether it normalises in Q2.
Deposit growth of about 30% with CASA held at 21% and FD costs about 8.1%; deposit roll-overs may reprice lower but are a constraint.
Dependence on one-off PSL income and CGFMU claims for profitability; the remaining claim is small, but about INR135–150 crore is claimable later.
Rising inflation and geopolitical disruption were flagged as possible pressure on collections, though management said stress is not expected in the next six months.
Tier 1 capital raise not finalised; Tier 2 raise was expected to close this quarter.
summary.management_tone: Confident on asset quality and collections, but cautious on growth and the MFI cycle. Management was explicit that Q2 will be weaker because PSL income falls away, and it did not commit to a higher ROE. On the CV PAR and the insurance-claim questions, answers were detailed and specific.
key_quotes: It is extremely important that we do not really take this as a reveal of the cycle and go aggressive.
The focus is at whatever we do, can every improvement be sustainable quarter-on-quarter?
We are not really to kind of guiding higher ROE at this point of time.
